what: The rounded curve at section boundaries swells the faster you scroll — each frame it follows the scrolled distance divided by 25 (max 1) at .1 per step, interpolating the path from its initial shape to the swollen shape, and once scrolling stops the velocity decays by ×.9 each frame so it slowly settles. For the rounded top edge of a navy band · the wave boundary below a photo

options.div: Scroll distance per frame to fill the share to 1 (px), default 25 — 30 for the curve under the photo
options.lerp: Ratio that follows the share (per frame), default .1
options.decay: Rate at which speed decays (per frame), default .9

use: <svg data-fx="speed-swell-edge" data-fx-speed-swell-edge="div: 25" viewBox="0 0 1440 247" preserveAspectRatio="none"><path data-fx-part="path" d="Initial shape" data-to="Inflated form (same node structure)"/></svg>
note: The original joins two shapes with MorphSVG — this part interpolates two paths with the same node structure number by number, so when the shapes differ the node counts are matched when drawing. Speed is the distance scrolled per frame rather than the Lenis value, so the same result comes out with or without Lenis

from.where: index.html rounded edge above the navy area (.lp-divider — speed/25 · lerp .1) and the curve below the building photo (.lp-divimg__curve — speed/30) — original MorphSVGPlugin + Lenis velocity
